page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.large is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with two dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache. It incorporates hardware instruction support for AVX, AVX-512 (including AVX512F and AVX512_VNNI), and AES cryptographic extensions. The system provides 8.0 GB of memory, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage and operates with a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark assessments show moderate single-thread capabilities paired with constrained parallel throughput due to the dual-thread single-core topology. In Geekbench testing, the instance achieved an average single-core score of 1163.0, but its multi-core score of 1381.0 sits in the bottom decile compared to higher-core instances. Stress-ng returned 1304.88 for single-core execution and 1735.44 for multi-core compute. Memory benchmarks reflect modest throughput, measuring 13.82 GB/sec for uncached 256MB read operations and 11.50 GB/sec for uncached write operations. PassMark tests produced an overall CPU score of 2147.33 and a database operations score of 722.46. High-throughput serving metrics recorded 1.68 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.96 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g6.large represents an entry-level tier for applications requiring dedicated Intel Xeon execution threads without paying for multi-socket core density. The primary tradeoff lies in the absence of integrated local NVMe storage and entry-level 1 Gbps networking, which mandates reliance on attached cloud block storage. As a balanced general-purpose configuration, it is suited for lightweight workloads including low-traffic web serving, small background workers, staging environments, basic microservices, and lightweight caching nodes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.large is a general-purpose virtual instance configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single hyper-threaded physical core on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization, it includes AVX-512 and AES instructions, 8.0 GB of system memory, no local disk storage, and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the middle 50% for single-core Geekbench performance (1163.0), though overall multi-threaded metrics remain modest due to the 2-vCPU hardware footprint. Memory throughput reaches 13.82 GB/sec for large uncached reads, while static web serving throughput registers at 1.96 GB/sec. Offering a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory allocation, the ecs.g6.large is positioned for lightweight general-purpose workloads such as low-traffic web backends, small Redis caching instances, continuous integration workers, and staging deployments.
